canonical_topic: ISDA and the ISDA Master Agreement
definition: ISDA (International Swaps and Derivatives Association) is an international trade association of major institutions active in privately negotiated derivatives. The ISDA Agreement is a standard set of clauses used in almost all OTC contracts; because all contracts referencing the master agreement share the same clauses, updates to the master agreement propagate to every referencing contract without renegotiation. Its most important clause is the netting-of-positions provision, which substantially reduces counterparty risk in privately negotiated derivatives deals.
core_idea: The ISDA master agreement standardizes OTC derivatives documentation so that legal/regulatory updates apply market-wide without bilateral renegotiation, and its netting provision is the key mechanism that tames OTC counterparty risk.
key_points: ISDA is a trade association, not a regulator or exchange.
The master agreement's clauses can be updated to meet changing regulatory environments across all referencing contracts at once.
Netting of positions is called out as the single most important clause because it materially reduces counterparty risk.
relationships: Directly underlies how Forwards and other OTC contracts manage counterparty credit risk, in contrast to exchange margin.
trading_implications: Netting under an ISDA agreement reduces the effective counterparty exposure between two OTC counterparties, which is a key reason OTC forwards remain viable despite lacking exchange-style margin.
